acceptanceCriteriaMapping.note: The authoritative doc has two numbered lists: numbered sections (1-24) and the 'Acceptance Criteria' list (1-20). References here mean the Acceptance Criteria list unless they say 'section'. dailyProofCycleCompletion demonstrates ONE controlled cycle, end to end, for Project A: Spec 147 -> 145 -> 141 -> 146 -> 144 -> 142/138 -> ADOS execution -> independent Codex reviewer resolved for that run -> real ADOS run-level completion reflected by the office -> Project A's task closed to 'completed' via the existing operator transition -> publication-readiness gate for that SAME bound execution (criteria 1-17, 19-20; office lifecycle section 12). Project A's request/preparation/execution is machine-bound (projectA.durableAdosRunIdBinding) to the durable ADOS run this verification session's own candidate is running under, so its implementer/reviewer are asserted equal to that run's own recorded agentAssignment, and its publication-readiness leg is derived from that same run's real durable validation/review records via the shared spec148DurableAlignment.js helper (validationPlan.js isFinalValidationSatisfied / validationPolicy.js targetsMatch / reviewConvergence.js computeConvergenceStatus), exercised unconditionally in both directions by spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts. Criteria 19-20 are met for this candidate only when that real independent Codex review returns Approved at exact HEAD, which cannot be recorded inside the candidate under review - a standing gate re-derived per candidate, not a frozen verdict; see publicationResult. Push, PR readiness, approval, merge, and remote deletion stay the human-only publication boundary. Never fabricated (section 18).
acceptanceCriteriaMapping.criterion11ExactHeadConvergence: Enforced from the real durable ADOS records (candidate.json / validation-runtime.json / review-runtime.json) by spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts: each of candidateMatchesHead / validatedMatchesHead / reviewedMatchesHead is DERIVED with the production comparator (validationPolicy.js targetsMatch) against `git rev-parse HEAD`, defaults false, and the convergence biconditional (computeConvergenceStatus == CONVERGED iff an Approved review is aligned on candidate == validated == reviewed == exact HEAD) runs UNCONDITIONALLY, both directions. Not simulated in-cycle with a hand-built object.
acceptanceCriteriaMapping.criterion19FullValidation: ADOS runs the full configured validation set against exact HEAD for every candidate and writes durable validation-runtime.json; production's validationPlan.js isFinalValidationSatisfied (validationPolicy.js targetsMatch) at the orchestrateCommand.js final-verification stage routes a target mismatch back to fix instead of the human merge gate. For ANY durable validation-runtime.json with status PASS - regardless of whether it aligns to exact HEAD - spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts asserts that all six configured commands ran, exited 0, did not time out, and that the worktree was unmutated (head_before == head_after); a stale PASS still carries the complete list, so this is not HEAD-alignment gated. Only status BLOCK (truncated command list) and an absent record escape the completeness assertion; the convergence biconditional still runs in both and refuses to converge. See dailyProofCycleCompletion.fullConfiguredValidationResult.

dailyProofCycleCompletion.note: ONE controlled cycle demonstrated end to end for Project A, whose request/preparation/execution is machine-bound (projectA.durableAdosRunIdBinding) to the durable ADOS run this verification session's own candidate is running under. The deterministic harness drives Spec 147 -> 145 -> 141 -> 146 -> 144 -> 142/138 -> ADOS execution with the real services; per authoritative requirement 23 the ImplementerRuntimeProvider process spawn is the only injectable adapter. The same test continues past execution: it resolves the independent reviewer from the run's own durable implementer id (Claude -> distinct Codex, via the real roleResolver.js), asserted equal to the bound run's own recorded agentAssignment, then ATTEMPTS to close Project A's task to terminal 'completed'. Execution-level completion (execution.evidence.completed true, distinct from ImplementerRuntimeStatus 'Completed', which means only 'subprocess exited') drives production's deriveExternalProjectAdosRunStatus to run stage 'Completed' and the Spec 144 active-execution count to 0, but Finding 2 (independent review, post-round-18) means it is no longer sufficient by itself to close the task: ProjectBacklogService.updateTask now REQUIRES publicationReadinessConfirmed - derived beforehand from this SAME bound execution's real durable ADOS records via the shared spec148DurableAlignment.js helper, not manually declared - for any task carrying an executionRunId, and refuses the transition (task stays in_progress) otherwise. There is still no AUTONOMOUS in_progress -> completed path; the operator's existing updateSelectedBacklogTaskFromInput call is the only route, but that call itself now enforces the gate. The candidate == validated == reviewed == exact HEAD + Approved-review publication gate cannot be carried on the in-office ExternalProjectAdosExecution records themselves (schema types those sub-stage flags as literal false); it is enforced by the production modules and exercised over this run's own durable ADOS records by both this test and spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts. Its honest current state is not-converged, so this cycle's completion attempt is REFUSED and the task remains in_progress (see publicationResult and spec148CandidatePublicationGate). Push, PR readiness, approval, merge, and remote deletion stay the human-only publication boundary.

This is the correct, stronger demonstration - a fabricated 'completed' here would contradict publicationResult below.

dailyProofCycleCompletion.convergenceBiconditional: spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts asserts, unconditionally and against the real durable ADOS records, that computeConvergenceStatus == CONVERGED iff an Approved review is aligned on candidate == validated == reviewed == exact HEAD; the negative branch pins the specific non-converged status (IN_PROGRESS for a 'Changes Requested' / trailing-SHA review, NOT_STARTED for a clean checkout) and asserts publicationResult stays a standing 'Blocked until ...' gate.
dailyProofCycleCompletion.fullConfiguredValidationResult: ADOS runs the full configured validation set (npm test, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build, npm run test:e2e:home-canvas, git diff --check, git diff --cached --check) against exact HEAD for every candidate and writes durable .agent-workflow/runs/148-.../validation-runtime.json. A standing gate, re-established per candidate, not a frozen snapshot. For ANY such record with status PASS - not only one naming exact HEAD - spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts asserts (never transcribed as a SHA literal) that all six configured commands ran, exited 0, did not time out, and head_before == head_after (worktree unmutated). Dropping the prior HEAD-alignment gate on this completeness assertion only strengthens it (a stale PASS still carries the complete list) and was the exact conditionality the independent review flagged. `validated_sha == git HEAD` stays a derivation input, not an unconditional assertion, because this suite runs as npm test = validation command #1. Two record states escape the completeness assertion, both safe: status BLOCK (a failed attempt, e.g. a host-suspension wall-clock timeout, writes a truncated command list - asserting it would deadlock recovery) and an absent record; the convergence biconditional still runs in both and refuses to converge.

spec148OwnCandidateGate.note: The publication-readiness leg of the SAME bound execution as simulatedProjectCycle (acceptance criteria 19-20; see projectA.durableAdosRunIdBinding), a standing per-candidate gate re-derived from durable state. Finding 2 (independent review, post-round-18) makes it a literal precondition of simulatedProjectCycle's task-closing transition, not merely a fact asserted beside it: ProjectBacklogService.updateTask requires publicationReadinessConfirmed for any task with an executionRunId. The in-office ExternalProjectAdosExecution records cannot carry these sub-stages themselves (schema literal false) - AutonomousCompanyOperationsE2E.test.ts asserts execution.reviewStarted / publishStarted / githubMutationStarted are false as an unconditional shape check in both run states, and derives this SAME execution's publication-readiness status from its bound durable ADOS records BEFORE attempting the task-closing transition, passing the result in as publicationReadinessConfirmed; today that is honestly not CONVERGED, production refuses the transition, and no repository/GitHub mutation occurred.
spec148OwnCandidateGate.validation -> exact HEAD: From durable ADOS state: tools/agent-workflow/spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts reads .agent-workflow/runs/148-.../{candidate,validation-runtime,review-runtime}.json, compares candidate/validated/reviewed SHA to `git rev-parse HEAD` with the SAME comparator (validationPolicy.js targetsMatch, reached via validationPlan.js isFinalValidationSatisfied at the orchestrateCommand.js final-verification stage), and runs the convergence biconditional UNCONDITIONALLY - an absent later-stage record derives that leg's match as false (never a skip), and a later-stage record present without its earlier sibling fails. ADOS re-establishes durable validation-runtime.json as a PASS per candidate; for ANY record with status PASS - regardless of HEAD alignment - the test asserts the full six-command configured set ran, exited 0, did not time out, and the worktree was unmutated (a stale PASS still carries the complete list; only BLOCK and absent escape it). NOTE: this suite runs inside `npm test` = validation command #1, so validation-runtime.json naming the current HEAD can only exist after this passes - that `validated_sha == HEAD` leg is a derivation input, not an unconditional assertion, and this constraint is stated, not hidden.
spec148OwnCandidateGate.exact HEAD -> publication gate: The gate runs through the real production modules in spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts, which executes the convergence biconditional over this run's durable ADOS records - candidate/validated/reviewed SHA alignment via the production comparator validationPolicy.js targetsMatch against real HEAD, carrying the real durable review decision - unconditionally in both directions, plus a real-SHA fixture triple and its refused variants (authoritative requirement 23: the review runtime is a process boundary, like the implementer spawn). CONVERGED only on an Approved review aligned on candidate == validated == reviewed == exact HEAD; for this candidate the durable review reads 'Changes Requested' while under review, so the gate is not converged (publicationResult). Push / approval / merge / remote deletion stay the human-only publication boundary. See spec148CandidatePublicationGate.

spec148CandidatePublicationGate.note: The final leg of the one demonstrated controlled cycle: review, validation, exact HEAD, publication gate. ADOS runs the full configured validation set and an independent Codex review against exact candidate HEAD for every candidate. This tracked artifact records no publish/merge/deploy verdict because committing it advances HEAD and would immediately stale a frozen verdict - the live per-candidate state lives in the durable .agent-workflow/runs/148-.../{candidate,validation-runtime,review-runtime}.json sources, gated in production by validationPlan.js isFinalValidationSatisfied (validationPolicy.js targetsMatch) at the orchestrateCommand.js final-verification stage and tools/agent-workflow/reviewConvergence.js computeConvergenceStatus. spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts exercises the convergence biconditional (candidate == validated == reviewed == exact HEAD + Approved review, both directions) over those durable records in every case, unconditionally, and additionally over a real-SHA fixture triple (authoritative requirement 23: the review runtime is a process boundary). For this candidate the durable review reads 'Changes Requested' while under review, so the gate is not converged (publicationResult). Push, PR readiness, approval, merge, and remote deletion are the human-only publication boundary and are not performed by the runtime (execution policy; the same boundary Specs 142-147 declare). Spec 148's production changes are two additive changes (durable-run-identity-from-execution-boundary, and a publication-readiness gate on task completion plus its manual-status-control resync) across 10 existing src/ modules total, plus an 18-line self-review/reviewer-availability guard in tools/agent-workflow/roleResolver.js (see nonInvocationsVerified.srcProductionSourceModifiedDetail); no second orchestration engine. The new tools/agent-workflow/spec148DurableAlignment.js is a read-only, test-only helper (see nonInvocationsVerified).
spec148CandidatePublicationGate.criterion19FullValidation: ADOS runs the full configured validation set against exact HEAD for every candidate (see dailyProofCycleCompletion.fullConfiguredValidationResult). For ANY durable validation-runtime.json with status PASS - not only one naming exact HEAD - spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts asserts (derived, never a SHA literal) all six commands ran, exited 0, did not time out, and left the worktree unmutated; only status BLOCK and an absent record escape that assertion.
spec148CandidatePublicationGate.criterion20ApprovedReview: The independent Codex review runs against exact candidate HEAD; computeConvergenceStatus reaches CONVERGED only on an Approved review aligned on candidate == validated == reviewed == exact HEAD (spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts, both directions, run unconditionally). Not fabricated here.

shaAlignment.note: Requirement 21 asks for candidate/validated/reviewed SHA 'where available' plus the exact-HEAD result. Two forms are recorded: (1) the LIVE per-candidate values are not transcribed as literals - a SHA for the candidate currently under review is stale the moment this evidence commit lands - they are resolved at validation/review time from durableSources below; (2) COMPLETED cycles are recorded as historical observations in observedCycles below (an already-finished candidate's SHAs are permanent branch history, never stale). Both test suites read durableSources and run the convergence biconditional over them: each of candidateMatchesHead / validatedMatchesHead / reviewedMatchesHead defaults false and is only raised by a present, format-valid, exact-HEAD-aligned record, so an absent record can never authorize CONVERGED. Pipeline order candidate -> validate -> review is a presence rule: a later-stage record present without its earlier sibling fails, not skips. spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts runs as validation command #1, so validated_sha === HEAD is a derivation input there (stated, not a hidden guard); the assertion is 'must not authorize publication'. The comparator is the production one (validationPolicy.js targetsMatch, reached via validationPlan.js isFinalValidationSatisfied at the orchestrateCommand.js final-verification stage).
shaAlignment.observedCyclesNote: Requirement 21 candidate/validated/reviewed SHA 'where available'. Each entry is a COMPLETED ADOS cycle as observed when this evidence was authored - a historical fact about an already-finished candidate, not a per-candidate verdict frozen ahead of the gate. Every recorded SHA is an ancestor-or-equal of branch HEAD (permanent history). spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts enforces the 40-hex + ancestor-or-equal shape and, whenever the durable review-runtime.json still names a recorded SHA, that its decision matches the recorded one - so these rows cannot be hand-forged to claim an outcome the durable record contradicts.

publicationResult: Blocked until ADOS records an Approved independent Codex review with candidateSha == validatedSha == reviewedSha == exact HEAD (reviewConvergence.js computeConvergenceStatus == CONVERGED). Standing per-candidate gate, not a frozen verdict: a durable Approved review of this exact candidate cannot precede its own approval, so no evidence committed with the candidate can assert it. spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts runs the gate unconditionally over this run's own durable ADOS records and a real-SHA fixture triple, proving CONVERGED is reachable for the Approved-and-aligned case without asserting this candidate has been approved.
